bounds.domain: One Worker CacheClient, two failure generations, two unique timer owners and two response slots. Production uses UUID identities and monotonically increasing in-memory generations. The bounded model can rearm at most twice.
bounds.atomicity: Relative timer expiry, durable publication and response delivery are distinct. A matching durable owner can publish readiness; only an exact current client generation can consume it. Lost acknowledgements fail closed. Restart preserves completed receipts and rearms an unfinished receipt with a new full wait. Old callbacks are retained as a conservative overapproximation after restart.
bounds.progress: Synchronous isAvailable can observe readiness without issuing a cache command, using the current request task registrar or native Worker waitUntil fallback. Progress assumes a stable generation, no further restart, fair relative timer completion, successful durable storage and an eventually acknowledged current-generation observation. Backend availability is not guaranteed.
bounds.conformance: Conformance executes production CacheClient and KV adapter plus gate/controller in real Workerd at compatibility date 2026-04-01. Node-only Wadis/Redis branches and unrelated database/funding recovery are rejecting fixture boundaries. Routine race tests scale only the cooldown to 500 ms. An additional production 60,000 ms run proves the actual relative delay across ordinary request completion and both wall-clock corrections.

limitations: The existing private INFERENCE_ADMISSION_GATES binding owns reserved cache-circuit:<UUID> identities. Only their POST /cache-circuit route enters the clock controller. Other identities cannot enter it; reserved identities cannot run tenant ledger routes. Public control Worker fetch is always 404. Other public application routes do not forward arbitrary object names or clock paths.

Synchronous isAvailable can observe readiness without issuing a cache command, using the current request task registrar or native Worker waitUntil fallback. Progress assumes a stable generation, no further restart, fair relative timer completion, successful durable storage and an eventually acknowledged current-generation observation. Backend availability is not guaranteed.

No migration, tenant ledger authority, durable alarm or Date/performance deadline is introduced. Runtime eviction can extend the wait; repeated restart, storage errors, missing bindings or lost acknowledgements may keep the circuit open. Object cleanup, transport reconnects, backend operations other than the linked receipt paths and unbounded concurrent callers remain outside this model.

assumptions: The failure generation is stable and no restart occurs. Arming, relative timer expiry, successful durable publication, current-generation receipt observation and synchronous probe are weakly fair.
A successful current-generation receipt observation is eventually possible. Storage/backend availability and a wall-clock deadline are not implied.
